messages:
maria: FYI customer t-acme-003 reports a spike of 429s + tail latency on /v1/generate since ~03:00 UTC. Customer says it started after a nightly job. Can someone triage? :thinking:

kai: Can you paste a sample request_id and a short curl? Also need the tenant id (confirmed t-acme-003) and approximate spike window.

maria: request_id=01FZ9QK2G. Here is a minimized curl they sent:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXXX" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: 01FZ9QK2G" \
  -d '{"model":"llama-2-13b-q4o","input":"summarize...","max_tokens":1024}'
```

Logs show repeated 429s with reason=quota_exceeded. Snippet: 

```
2026-03-16T03:07:12.123Z tenant=t-acme-003 route=/v1/generate req=01FZ9QK2G status=429 reason=quota_exceeded tokens=412
2026-03-16T03:07:13.004Z tenant=t-acme-003 route=/v1/generate req=01FZ9QK2H status=200 tokens=102
```

anya: Quick checklist: 1) confirm per-tenant token quota & any burst credits 2) inspect per-route QPS and token-rate heatmap 3) check limit_enforcer_events for whether the enforcer applied tenant or route rule 4) sample traces for 01FZ9QK2G. I spun up the dashboard panels you need: Observability > Limits > Tenant Snapshots (internal link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/limits).

jordan: Is this sure quota exhaustion and not a global concurrent limit or model-side throttling? The log reason says quota_exceeded but sometimes upstream model rejects and we map to 429.

anya: Good point. Run this query in our analytics cluster to attribute: 

```
SELECT ts, route, model, api_key_id, status_code, reason, tokens
FROM limit_enforcer_events
WHERE tenant_id='t-acme-003' AND ts >= '2026-03-16T03:00:00Z'
ORDER BY ts DESC
LIMIT 100;
```

Look for repeated api_key_id or a single route dominating tokens. If many small requests, it's a QPS issue; if large token counts, it's token quota.

kai: I pulled a quick aggregation for 03:00-03:15: tenant tokens=1.2M, 92% from route=/v1/embeddings (background job), only 5% from /v1/generate. So the embeddings job exhausted tenant quota and bumped other routes to 429. :eyes:

maria: Interesting — customer said nightly job was updated last week. They likely increased batch size.

anya: For next steps: - sample one of the embeddings requests (api_key_id XXXXXX) to confirm token count - create a per-route alert: trigger when tenant token rate > 300k tokens/min sustained 2m - add a short-term mitigation: grant a temporary burst credit or throttle embeddings job to a lower concurrency.

kai: Mitigation command I can run if you ok it: 

```
redwoodctl quotas adjust --tenant t-acme-003 --route /v1/embeddings --burst 500000 --duration 3600
```

This will add a 1-hour burst credit. Also setting a temporary circuit on that job's api_key_id will protect the rest of their routes.

jordan: Can we add an attribution panel to the tenant dashboard that breaks down top 10 api_key_id x route x model by tokens? That would make root-cause faster next time.

anya: Yep, added panel "Tenant Token Attribution (top 10)" and a compact sparklines row. I also updated alert rule: 

- name: tenant-token-surge-critical
- when: tenant.tokens_rate > 300000 for 2m
- notify: support/escalations + paging on P2

ops-bot: monitor:alert created tenant-token-surge-critical for t-acme-003 (id: alert-8732) :white_check_mark:

maria: I'll tell the customer: 1) we identified embeddings job as primary culprit 2) temporary burst credit applied 3) recommend they reduce batch_size / concurrency and we can advise an autoscaling config for Dedicated if they need consistent throughput.

kai: After they confirm reduction, we should revoke the burst credit and follow up with a billing/usage review in case they want a higher commit.

maria: Thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread updated with customer confirmation. :thumbsup:
